Subject: Post-call recap 28 TTFT & streaming SLOs (FinLytics)

Thanks again for your time this morning, Mia 28 great conversation and appreciate the clear product constraints. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can lock down scope for an SE deep-dive: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary objective: reduce perceived latency for live financial insights in the analyst UI. Streaming responses are required (chunked text updates) so users see partial results as they’re generated.
- Current client-side processing ~40ms median; target is the backend TTFT (time-to-first-token) to be low enough that combined client+server meets SLA.
- Rough traffic profile: peak concurrent users ~30 per analyst workspace, expected max concurrency (across region) ~50, peak sustained QPS for LLM generate calls ~200.

Stated SLO targets (please confirm or update):
- TTFT (p95): <= 100 ms (goal) 28 fallback acceptable up to 120 ms (p95)
- Chunk cadence for streaming: flush every 150283300 ms; subsequent chunks should be visible within 250 ms of generation
- Max chunk size: ~2KB (to keep UI updates snappy)
- Throughput: sustain 200 rps for generation paths with concurrency up to 50
- Availability: best-effort for hosted; will discuss Dedicated if stricter SLOs required

Proposed next steps
1) Rishi/Dev: run a short synthesis of what our infra would look like to meet the above (model variant, expected TTFT ranges, batching tradeoffs).
2) Mia/FinLytics: confirm the p95 TTFT target and whether WebSocket is required vs SSE.
3) I’ll attach the SLO worksheet we talked through; please add any measurements you have (client latencies, observed backend latencies).
4) Schedule 60-min SE session 281 goal: propose configuration and an initial test plan.

Attachments: SLO_requirements.xlsx (worksheet to collect measured latencies), streaming_cadence_diagram.png

Thanks 281 I’ll coordinate availability for next week once we get confirmation on the TTFT target and streaming transport preference.

Thanks Marissa 28 that matches what we discussed. A couple notes to clarify our constraints: 

- We can commit to the p95 TTFT <= 100 ms target for the initial rollout. Ideally < 90 ms. If you can hit 100 ms p95 in a hosted proof-of-concept we’ll be in good shape.
- We prefer SSE as the initial transport (simplicity + firewall friendliness), but we may need WebSocket later for mobile clients.
- Peak concurrency across our busiest region typically hits ~30 concurrent generation streams; we expect short bursts to 45 but they’re < 5 mins.
- Payload characteristics: average prompt size ~600 tokens, average response length ~150 tokens (streaming chunks should begin delivering within the first 50 tokens).

I’ve attached a small csv with our client-side timing samples (client_times.csv) to the Hub drive (link below). Can Rishi/Dev propose a preliminary config assuming an open-source LLM in the 72813B parameter range?

Link: https://drive.google.com/finlytics/client_times.csv

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap 28 TTFT & streaming SLOs (FinLytics)

Hi Mia 28 thanks for the details, very helpful. A few technical clarifications and what we’ll deliver in the SE session: 

1) Measurement approach‑ We recommend measuring TTFT at the edge (Redwood edge or your CDN) and at the model container. For p95 TTFT you should exclude client-side parsing/DOM render times so we can isolate server contribution. We’ll run synthetic load with your avg prompt sizes and response token lengths to estimate p50/p95 TTFT and token throughput.

2) Expected numbers & levers‑ With a 72813B float16/INT8 quantized model on a single A100-class or equivalent instance, we typically observe TTFT (cold KV+prefill) in the 6028140 ms range depending on prompt length and KV cache hit. With prefix caching and warm KV hit, p95 can be brought < 100 ms.
- Batching: increases throughput but can add TTFT tail; for interactive streaming we favor small batching windows (~52810 ms) + priority lanes for low-latency streams.
- KV/prefix cache: big win if you have repeated analyst queries or system prompts.

3) Streaming cadence recommendations‑ SSE is fine 28 we’ll recommend server-side flush cadence every 150 ms during active generation. If chunk size grows beyond 22834KB, we’ll throttle chunking to keep UI smooth. For mobile/WebSocket we can do the same cadence. Also enable keep-alive pings to avoid mid-session connection close on some enterprise proxies.

4) Test plan deliverables (what we’ll produce)
- Synthetic p50/p95 TTFT and per-token latency curves for the proposed model variants
- Concurrency/load patterns to validate bursts to 45 with graceful degradation
- Config notes: batching window, KV cache policy, candidate model variants (7B/13B), expected cost/throughput numbers

Next steps: I’ll put together a short config doc prior to our call. Can you share a representative prompt and the client timing CSV link so we can incorporate realistic traces?

28 Rishi
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
